thread:
ina.finance: Alert: Velox Diagnostics filed a formal billing query. Invoice INV-5408 shows reserved commit lines but customer claims they were charged burst rates. They attached evidence showing reserved_pool_id=rp-88 on invoice, but their account shows no active binding for May.
marco.ops: Can you attach invoice + provisioning audit? Also possible this is the misassignment bug we saw in the tenant-mapper job.
billing-bot: Invoice INV-5408 uploaded: https://invoices.redwood/INV-5408.pdf
billing-bot: Metering snapshot: customer_id=cust_velox, committed_hours=0, burst_tokens=1,900,220, reserved_pool_on_invoice=rp-88
marco.ops: Running provisioning audit query now:
```
SELECT customer_id, reserved_pool_id, event_time
FROM provisioning.audit
WHERE reserved_pool_id='rp-88' AND date(event_time) BETWEEN '2026-05-01' AND '2026-05-31';
```
marco.ops: Query output: rows -> (cust_ring, rp-88, 2026-04-30T23:58:12Z), (cust_ring, rp-88, 2026-05-01T00:00:05Z)
rachel.sales: Wait — rp-88 belongs to RingBio (cust_ring). Velox (cust_velox) is listed on invoice but provisioning shows rp-88 was bound to cust_ring during May. That suggests tenant-mapper assigned the pool ID incorrectly on the invoice rendering.
nina.finance: Econ check: Velox billed burst=$18,200; expected reserved billing would be $9,700. Delta = $8,500. RingBio apparently got reserved buckets charged to their commitment (so we underbilled them relative to true usage?) Need to confirm RingBio usage.
marco.ops: Running metering for cust_ring May:
```
SELECT sum(committed_hours) as committed, sum(burst_tokens) as burst
FROM metering.events
WHERE customer_id='cust_ring' AND month='2026-05';
```
marco.ops: Output: committed=720, burst=120,000. Looks like RingBio legitimately consumed from rp-88 and should be attributed. So the invoice rendering step added rp-88 to Velox invoice incorrectly.
tess.revenue: This is messy. Options: (1) reissue corrected invoice for Velox and attach ledger note; (2) issue an operational credit to Velox and correct RingBio's invoices if needed; (3) if RingBio was charged differently we may need cross-customer reconciliations. Legal likely needs to sign off on reissues. What's finance exposure?
nina.finance: If we reallocate Velox to reserved retroactively, customer would be owed $8,500. If we instead issue operational goodwill credit, recommend cap = $10,000 to cover rounding and audit requests. However, RingBio could argue they've been overcharged if their reserved usage changed — but our metering shows they consumed the reserved capacity, so no recredit there. This is primarily an invoicing/rendering error.
rachel.sales: Velox is a strategic account; CS is pushing for a corrected invoice for their auditors. They prefer a formal corrected invoice + ledger note over a credit.
legal-bot: Reissuing invoices requires contract review if material (> $5k) and a signed memo from customer; else a ledger adjustment may suffice. Standard practice: reissue only if customer insists for audit.
tess.revenue: I need explicit approval to proceed with a corrected invoice or, alternatively, I'll approve a goodwill credit up to $10,000 if ops certifies this was rendering-only and not a provisioning failure. Please reply with "approve-corrected" or "approve-credit".
marco.ops: Confirming root cause: tenant-mapper template used stale mapping due to cache invalidation bug during 2026-05-01 deploy. Rendering claimed rp-88 on Velox invoice though provisioning bindings were correct. Patch merged to fix cache invalidation; runbook entry added.
tess.revenue: Given ops confirmation and the customer's auditor request, I approve reissuing a corrected invoice. Replying: approve-corrected.
nina.finance: Noted. We'll prepare corrected invoice INV-5408-R1, issue ledger note: "Corrected invoice due to rendering error: reserved_pool mislabel. No change to RingBio metering." Also create adjustment ADJ-2026-512 to reflect the customer-facing refund amount $8,500 if Velox already paid burst. Finance to coordinate with AR for refund or credit application.
billing-bot: Creating ledger entry placeholder: ADJ-2026-512 | customer: cust_velox | amount: -8500 | reason: invoice_correction_rendering_error | linked_invoice: INV-5408
rachel.sales: I'll notify customer and CS: "We've identified an invoicing rendering issue that misattributed reserved pool on your May invoice. We're issuing a corrected invoice and attaching a ledger note for your auditors. Expect corrected document within 48 hours; funds will be applied as account credit unless you request refund."
marco.ops: Patch deployed; cache invalidation test added to CI and a monitoring alert on mismatched reserved_pool_id between metering and invoice rendering. Runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/invoice-render-cache-fix
nina.finance: I'll attach ADJ-2026-512 to the corrected invoice workflow and route to AR for processing. Legal: please hold signature unless customer requests a reissued signed invoice.
legal-bot: Acknowledged. If customer demands signed corrected invoice for audit, we'll route contract team. Otherwise ledger note and corrected PDF are fine.
tess.revenue: Closing: approve-corrected. Please add the audit trail and postmortem note to the ticket.
nina.finance: Thanks. Action items: (1) issue INV-5408-R1, (2) post ADJ-2026-512 in ledger, (3) CS notification sent, (4) ops monitoring + runbook. Closing thread when PDF and ledger entry finalized.
